**Answer: Pennsylvania** – with the highest per‑unit visitor‑spending among the Pennsylvania‑bordering states that meet the 10‑site minimum.

---

| State | Official NPS units (per NPS “state” page) | 2023 Total Visitor Spending (NPS Visitor Spending Effects PDF) | Visitor‑Spending per Unit |
|-------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Pennsylvania** | 19 units | **$426.3 M** | **$22.4 M per unit** |
| Maryland | 18 units | **$329.3 M** | **$18.3 M per unit** |

**Sources**

| Data Point | Source |
|------------|--------|
| *Pennsylvania – 19 NPS units* | “Pennsylvania (U.S. National Park Service)” – NPS state page: “**19 National Parks**” (link: https://www.nps.gov/state/pa/index.htm) |
| *Pennsylvania – 2023 visitor‑spending $426.3 M* | “2023 National Park Visitor Spending Effects” PDF – Table showing Pennsylvania 8 300 004 visits and $426.3 M economic benefit (link: https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf) |
| *Maryland – 18 NPS units* | “Maryland (U.S. National Park Service)” – NPS state page: “**18 National Parks**” (link: https://www.nps.gov/state/md/index.htm) |
| *Maryland – 2023 visitor‑spending $329.3 M* | Same PDF as above – Maryland line $329.3 M (link: https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf) |

**Why Pennsylvania?**

- Pennsylvania meets the 10‑unit requirement (19 NPS units).  
- It also has the highest *per‑unit* total visitor spending: $426.3 M ÷ 19 = **$22.4 M per NPS unit.**  
- Maryland, the other qualifying neighbor, has $329.3 M ÷ 18 = **$18.3 M per unit**, lower than Pennsylvania’s figure.

Thus, among the states bordering Pennsylvania with at least 10 National Park Service sites, **Pennsylvania is the state that brings in the most money from total visitor spending per National Park Site** (2023 data).

**Answer: Pennsylvania** – with the highest per‑unit visitor‑spending among the Pennsylvania‑bordering states that meet the 10‑site minimum.

---

| State | Official NPS units (per NPS “state” page) | 2023 Total Visitor Spending (NPS Visitor Spending Effects PDF) | Visitor‑Spending per Unit |
|-------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Pennsylvania** | 19 units | **$426.3 M** | **$22.4 M per unit** |
| Maryland | 18 units | **$329.3 M** | **$18.3 M per unit** |

**Sources**

| Data Point | Source |
|------------|--------|
| *Pennsylvania – 19 NPS units* | “Pennsylvania (U.S. National Park Service)” – NPS state page: “**19 National Parks**” (link: https://www.nps.gov/state/pa/index.htm) |
| *Pennsylvania – 2023 visitor‑spending $426.3 M* | “2023 National Park Visitor Spending Effects” PDF – Table showing Pennsylvania 8 300 004 visits and $426.3 M economic benefit (link: https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf) |
| *Maryland – 18 NPS units* | “Maryland (U.S. National Park Service)” – NPS state page: “**18 National Parks**” (link: https://www.nps.gov/state/md/index.htm) |
| *Maryland – 2023 visitor‑spending $329.3 M* | Same PDF as above – Maryland line $329.3 M (link: https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf) |

**Why Pennsylvania?**

- Pennsylvania meets the 10‑unit requirement (19 NPS units).  
- It also has the highest *per‑unit* total visitor spending: $426.3 M ÷ 19 = **$22.4 M per NPS unit.**  
- Maryland, the other qualifying neighbor, has $329.3 M ÷ 18 = **$18.3 M per unit**, lower than Pennsylvania’s figure.

Thus, among the states bordering Pennsylvania with at least 10 National Park Service sites, **Pennsylvania is the state that brings in the most money from total visitor spending per National Park Site** (2023 data).
